title: Daily Health Briefing
intro: Good morning! Today's digest spans your five tracked topics — anti-aging (systemic and skin), HIIT for women, pelvic floor training, HER2+/TP53 breast cancer, and sleep. Findings are drawn from recent, reputable sources (PubMed, JAMA Network, NIH/ClinicalTrials.gov, Nature, AASM, and peer-reviewed journals), with citations linked as chips under each section. Informational only — talk to a clinician before acting on anything here.

sections.topic: Anti-Aging — Longevity Drugs, Supplements, Topicals & Devices
sections.body:
Two fronts this week: **systemic** longevity interventions (still biomarker-stage), and **skin** interventions where the human RCT data is actually stronger.

**Systemic (drugs & supplements):**

- **mTOR inhibitors — dose-finding, not proof yet.** The NIH-linked **RESTOR** trial (NCT06658093) is testing rapamycin *and* everolimus in healthy older adults to find doses that safely dial back mTOR toward youthful levels — explicitly determining **sex-specific** dosing, since the optimal dose in women may differ from men. This is still early: the completed **PEARL** trial (129 adults, weekly rapamycin) established a reassuring safety profile but was **not powered** to prove it slows aging.
- **Urolithin A for "inflammaging."** A 2025 *Nature Aging* randomized, placebo-controlled trial (50 middle-aged adults, 1,000 mg/day for 4 weeks) found the mitophagy inducer **urolithin A** expanded less-exhausted, naive-like CD8⁺ T cells and improved immune-cell mitochondrial function — mechanistic support for countering age-related immune decline.

**Skin (topicals & devices):**

- **Microneedling + antioxidants beats microneedling alone.** A 2026 double-blind, split-face RCT (31 adults) showed adding a **vitamin C + E + ferulic acid** serum to microneedling roughly tripled wrinkle-scale improvement (**23.9% vs 6.8%**) and markedly improved elasticity (**39% vs 6.8%**) versus placebo over 12 weeks.
- **Retinoids remain the topical workhorse**, and **red-light photobiomodulation** (≈630–660 nm) has randomized support for reducing wrinkles — though a 2025 expert consensus cautions that protocols vary and many device studies are small.

Practical framing: for **skin**, consistent retinoid + antioxidant + SPF regimens have the best evidence; for **systemic** longevity, expect **modest** effects and treat single-supplement "longevity" claims skeptically.

sections.body:
The consistent 2025–2026 message: HIIT is a **time-efficient** driver of cardio fitness and fat loss for women — but expect **recomposition more than scale change**, and pair it with strength work.

- **Recreationally active women.** A 2025 systematic review & meta-analysis (*Scientific Reports*, 15 studies, 304 women, ~25 yrs) found HIIT significantly improved **VO₂max/VO₂peak** and reduced **body-fat percentage**, but did **not** significantly change total body mass or fat mass — i.e., you may look leaner before the scale moves.
- **Cardio & BMI wins.** A 2025 meta-analysis of 19 cycling-HIIT RCTs (527 adults) found HIIT **matched MICT** for body composition and **outperformed** it for **VO₂peak** (and for lowering BMI in people with obesity) in a fraction of the time.
- **Older women.** A 2026 RCT (*Women*, MDPI) of supervised HIIT (3×/week) reported significant gains in **aerobic capacity, lower-limb strength, and mobility (Timed Up-and-Go)**, drops in **body-fat and visceral-fat** indices, and better quality of life — with **no major adverse events**.

Bottom line: intensity delivers the cardio/metabolic payoff; **add resistance training**, progress volume gradually, and keep recovery adequate.

sections.body:
**Pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT)** keeps proving its value as a **first-line**, low-risk option for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) — both before surgery and during pregnancy.

- **Before surgery, it can change the plan.** A 2026 RCT (90 women awaiting mid-urethral sling surgery) found **6 weeks of intensive preoperative PFMT** produced large improvements in muscle strength (Modified Oxford, *d* = 0.85) and incontinence severity (*d* = 0.90) vs. education alone — and in **43% of participants the planned surgery was postponed**. A strong case for trying structured PFMT first.
- **In pregnancy, it prevents postpartum leakage.** The multicenter **PEFLOW** trial (*JAMA Network Open*, 764 first-time mothers) found an in-pregnancy pelvic-floor workout **cut SUI at 6 weeks postpartum to 8.7% vs 13.9%** and more than doubled the share of women with strong pelvic-floor muscle scores.

Key point: **correct technique and consistency beat sheer reps.** Confirm activation with a clinician or biofeedback; supervised, progressive programs generally outperform casual, unsupervised ones.

sections.topic: HER2+ / TP53 (p53) Breast Cancer — Emerging Options & "Alternative" Cautions
sections.body:
For HER2-positive, often **TP53/p53-altered** breast cancer, the honest read is: genuine *alternative* (in-place-of-standard) cures **don't have supporting evidence** and can be harmful — but the **targeted science aimed squarely at the p53 pathway** is advancing.

- **A drug that reactivates mutant p53.** **Rezatapopt (PC14586)** is a first-in-class p53 *reactivator* selective for the **TP53 Y220C** mutation. In the phase-1 **PYNNACLE** experience (published in *NEJM* in 2026), heavily pretreated patients responded, and in the small breast-cancer subset **3 of 8 evaluable patients had confirmed partial responses**. The phase-2 **breast-cancer cohort (NCT04585750)** is enrolling.
- **Exploiting the HER2 + p53 combination.** Preclinical work shows **HER2;p53 co-mutant** tumors become especially sensitive to the **TOP1-inhibitor payload in trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)**; **neratinib + T-DXd** is now in an NCI-sponsored trial (NCT05372614).
- **On "alternative" and supplement approaches.** Use integrative options only as **oncologist-coordinated add-ons**, never substitutes — some supplements carry real **interaction, bleeding, or toxicity** risks with targeted therapy.

Important framing: rezatapopt and the T-DXd strategy are **investigational**; discuss genomic testing (including germline TP53) and trial eligibility with your oncology team.

sections.body:
For restless or fragmented sleep, 2025–2026 guidance still puts **behavioral therapy ahead of pills and supplements**.

- **CBT-I is the anchor.** The AASM's 2026 clinical practice guideline on *combination* therapy concluded **CBT-I alone is the most effective first-line treatment**; adding medication may modestly help specific outcomes (like total sleep time), but combination is **not** better than CBT-I by itself.
- **If medication is needed, choose wisely.** The 2025 **VA/DoD** guideline recommends behavioral therapy first, and — for short-term use with a deprescribing plan — favors **low-dose doxepin** or **dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs)** while advising **against** routine antihistamines, benzodiazepines, trazodone, and melatonin for chronic insomnia.

Supplements, honestly graded:

- **L-theanine:** a 2025 meta-analysis (19 trials, ~900 people) found small but significant improvements in **sleep-onset latency, daytime function, and subjective quality** at **200–450 mg/day** — best for sleep quality, not sleep *duration*.
- **Magnesium:** a 2026 systematic review rated the evidence **low/very-low certainty** and not sufficient for routine use, though a bisglycinate RCT showed a **modest** insomnia-severity benefit, especially in those with low dietary magnesium.
- **Ashwagandha:** a meta-analysis of 5 RCTs suggests **≥600 mg/day for ≥8 weeks** improves subjective sleep quality, onset latency, and efficiency — most in diagnosed insomnia.

Best-practice habits: keep a **fixed wake time**, reserve the bed for sleep only, dim lights and cut screens during wind-down, and if disrupted sleep persists beyond a few weeks, see a provider to rule out **sleep apnea / restless legs** and consider **CBT-I**.
